"""Colon detector for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3200.

The component is a colon detector. At a token that is a colon (':', the fullwidth '：',
or a colon fused with a newline, quote or bracket) it writes a negative value, and it is
close to zero at every other token. The size depends on the colon's form: a plain colon
that introduces a status line, an error or a label is strongly negative; code syntax
('::', ':=', '://') is nearly zero.

Measured on training text, the mean activation is about -1.5 for ':' and -1.1 over all
colon tokens, with large spread (std about 1.1) that depends on the words before the colon.
Non-colon tokens average about 0 with spread about 0.3 that this program does not model.
"""

READS = ()

# Mean activation at each colon form, measured on training rows.
COLON_VALUE = {
    ":": -1.5,
    "：": -1.7,
    ":\n": -1.0,
    ":\n\n": -0.8,
    " :": -0.8,
    '":': -0.8,
    "):": -1.2,
    "::": 0.0,
    ":=": -0.2,
    "://": -0.4,
}
OTHER_COLON = -1.1  # any other colon-bearing token
NON_COLON = 0.0  # every other token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if ":" not in tok and "：" not in tok:
        return carry, NON_COLON
    return carry, COLON_VALUE.get(tok, OTHER_COLON)

"""Noun-compound heads, as a negative push on the MLP layer-15 down-projection component 3201.

What it does: the component is mostly quiet, but it goes clearly negative on a common noun that
directly follows another common noun inside the same document, i.e. the head of a two-noun term
("bank" in "capacitor bank", "call" in "API call", "section" in "tissue section", "area" in
"growing area"). The push is strongest for generic, abstract or process-like heads (system,
level, process, method, rate, layer, project, call) and weaker for heads that name places,
substances or amounts. It is stronger again when a determiner ("the", "a", "her", ...) opens the
noun phrase within the last few words. Everything else predicts 0.

This is a readable approximation: it explains only a few percent of the variance. Most of the
activation is in rare, large negative spikes on particular words in particular contexts, which
no word class captures. A per-token lookup table would explain a little more, but would be a
list of token ids with no concept behind it.
"""

import wordnet

READS = ()

# WordNet lexicographer classes for generic, abstract or process-like nouns (the strong heads).
GENERIC = frozenset({
    "noun.process", "noun.cognition", "noun.act", "noun.event", "noun.attribute", "noun.state",
    "noun.relation", "noun.phenomenon", "noun.group", "noun.object", "noun.artifact",
    "noun.possession", "noun.Tops", "noun.food", "noun.animal",
})
# Classes for places, substances, amounts and communication: heads of these push less.
MASS = frozenset({"noun.substance", "noun.quantity", "noun.location", "noun.communication"})
DETERMINERS = frozenset({
    "the", "a", "an", "her", "his", "its", "their", "my", "our", "your", "this", "that",
    "these", "those", "each", "every", "some",
})


def _word(text):
    return text.strip().lower()


def _is_noun(word):
    return word.isalpha() and "noun" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    words = [_word(s) for s in prefix.token_strings[-5:]]
    if len(words) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        return carry, 0.0
    head, modifier = words[-1], words[-2]
    if not (_is_noun(head) and _is_noun(modifier)):
        return carry, 0.0
    value = -0.2
    cats = wordnet.categories(head, "noun")
    if cats & GENERIC and not cats & MASS:
        value -= 0.2
    if any(w in DETERMINERS for w in words[:-2]):
        value -= 0.3
    return carry, value

"""Component layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3202 (a near-dead, diffuse readout).

What it is: one rank-one piece of layer 15's MLP down projection. Its read vector is
dominated by MLP hidden unit 3202 (about 0.47 of its weight, ~43% of its squared norm),
with the rest spread thinly over ~6000 other hidden units. Its causal importance is ~0 on
every token, and switching it off changes the model's output by almost nothing.

What it does on tokens: its activation is a diffuse signal with mean about -0.05 and
standard deviation 0.28. Nothing simple predicts it: token identity, previous token,
token class (digits, punctuation, words, Han characters, newlines) and position in the
document each explain under 0.1% of its variance on held-out data. So this program does not
try to model the signal. It predicts the average value everywhere, and 0 at the first token
of each document (where the activation is ~0).
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = -0.052  # the component's mean activation over positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """The average activation, except 0 at a document's first token."""
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    first_of_document = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first_of_document else MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3204 (about half of this component's variance comes from that
one unit; the rest is spread thinly over many): a weak "a correlative pair is still open"
signal.

What it does: the component goes negative inside a pair that is waiting for its second
half, as in "both X and Y", "neither X nor Y", "either X or Y", "between X and Y". It is
most negative on the word right after "neither" or "both", and milder after "either" or
"between". A pair counts as open from its opener until a closer ("and", "or", "nor",
"to") or a new document. Everywhere else it predicts 0.

It captures only a small part of the variance: most of it sits in rare, large,
context-specific spikes that no short rule reproduces.
"""

READS = ()

OPENERS = {"both": -1.1, "neither": -2.6, "either": -0.5, "between": -0.35}
CLOSERS = {"and", "or", "nor", "to", "et", "und"}
OPEN_VALUE = -0.15  # tokens later inside an open pair


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: (document id, opener word or None, tokens since the opener)
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        opener, since = None, 0
    else:
        _, opener, since = carry
    value = 0.0
    if word in CLOSERS:
        opener = None
    elif opener is not None:
        value = OPENERS[opener] if since == 0 else OPEN_VALUE
        since += 1
    if word in OPENERS:
        opener, since = word, 0
    return (doc, opener, since), value

"""Layer 15 MLP down-projection, component 3205: a "need / lack" detector.

The component goes strongly negative on words that say something is needed, required or
missing ("need", "needed", "missing", "required", "necessary", "lack"), and on their
French, Russian, German and Chinese equivalents (besoin, нужн-, benöt-, 需要, 欠 ...).
Obligation words ("should", "must", "want", "important", "enough") are weakly negative.
The response is cut to about a fifth when a negation or condition comes just before the
word ("do not need", "no need", "if necessary"). The token right after a need-word
carries about 0.3 of that word's value. Every other token predicts 0.

Why: the big negative spikes of this component sit on need/lack words; switching it off
moves the model's next-token predictions, and this program keeps most of that effect. Most
of the remaining variance is diffuse token-level noise a short program cannot capture.
"""

READS = ()

NEED = {
    "need": -4.0, "needs": -4.0, "needed": -5.0, "needing": -4.7,
    "missing": -4.7, "lack": -2.2, "lacks": -4.0, "lacking": -3.0,
    "require": -1.1, "requires": -1.6, "required": -2.2,
    "necessary": -2.5, "essential": -1.4,
    "besoin": -5.0, "нужн": -6.0, "необходим": -5.5, "требуется": -3.0,
    "benöt": -6.0, "需要": -2.4, "必要": -2.6, "欠": -6.0, "不足": -3.9,
}
OBLIGATION = {"should": -0.5, "must": -0.5, "want": -0.5, "enough": -1.0, "important": -0.6}
NEGATION = {"not", "no", "n't", "'t", "’t", "never", "nor", "without", "if", "unless"}


def word_value(word):
    word = word.strip().lower()
    if word in NEED:
        return NEED[word]
    if word in OBLIGATION:
        return OBLIGATION[word]
    return 0.0


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    word = word_value(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    same_doc = [i for i in (t - 1, t - 2) if i >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[i] == prefix.document_ids[t]]
    prev1 = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if t - 1 in same_doc else ""
    prev2 = prefix.token_strings[-3].strip().lower() if t - 2 in same_doc else ""
    if word and (prev1 in NEGATION or prev2 in NEGATION):
        word *= 0.2
    before = word_value(prev1) * 0.3 if prev1 else 0.0
    return None, word + before

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3207 (through this component's read direction) as seen from the
token stream.

The component reads the MLP hidden state of layer 15 along one direction, which is almost
entirely hidden unit 3207, and writes it back into the residual stream with a small norm. Its
activation is close to zero at the first token of every document (where the MLP has nothing
to attend to yet) and otherwise a diffuse, slightly negative value with no clear dependence on
the current token, previous token, or position. The mean over ordinary tokens is about -0.048.

This program predicts that: 0 at the first token of each document, and the ordinary-token mean
everywhere else. It explains almost none of the variance, because the activation depends on
context that a token-level program cannot see.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN = -0.048  # mean activation at ordinary (non-document-initial) tokens


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    ids = prefix.document_ids
    first = len(ids) == 1 or ids[-1] != ids[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first else MEAN

"""Layer 15, MLP down_proj, component 3208.

What it does: a weak, mostly context-driven component. Its activation is near zero
almost everywhere (std 0.38) with rare large swings, and its largest share comes from
one MLP hidden unit (3208 of layer 15) whose value depends on the surrounding text
rather than on any fixed word. The only readable tendency found is a dip below zero
on words that set up a concession or report a failure, and on the next word after
them. This program predicts that dip and 0 everywhere else.

  - concession words ("despite", "though", "even", "regardless"): about -0.6
  - failure / invalidity words ("invalid", "incorrect", "illegal", "incomplete",
    "broken", "failed", "error", "exit", ...): about -0.34
  - "return" (an early return in error-handling code): about -0.57
  - the word right after one of the above: about -0.24

Why: these are the places where it is most negative. Token identity alone explains
about 2% of its variance on held-out rows, and these rules add well under 1%.
"""

READS = ()

CONCESSIVE = {"despite", "spite", "regardless", "though", "although", "even"}
FAILURE = {
    "invalid", "incorrect", "incorrectly", "illegal", "incomplete", "partial",
    "partially", "broken", "unsafe", "unused", "failed", "fail", "error", "warning",
    "exit", "unexpected", "inconsistent", "insufficient",
}
WEIGHT = {"concessive": -0.6, "failure": -0.34, "return": -0.57, "after": -0.24}


def word_of(token):
    return token.strip().lower()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    # carry: whether the previous token was a concession or failure word
    word = word_of(prefix.token_strings[-1])
    same_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    value = 0.0
    if carry and same_doc:
        value += WEIGHT["after"]
    if word in CONCESSIVE:
        value += WEIGHT["concessive"]
    elif word in FAILURE:
        value += WEIGHT["failure"]
    elif word == "return":
        value += WEIGHT["return"]
    flagged = word in CONCESSIVE or word in FAILURE
    return flagged, value

"""Predict the component's activation from the kind of the current token.

Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3209 is a diffuse readout of layer 15's
MLP hidden state. It has no trigger a person can name: its activation (std 0.35) is spread
over almost every token, and the best simple predictors found explain under 1% of its
variance. The one trend worth keeping is by token kind: words and numbers sit slightly
above zero, punctuation, spaces and line breaks slightly below. This program predicts the
mean activation of each kind, measured on 2 million training tokens.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN_BY_KIND = {
    "letter": 0.031,  # words, including Chinese characters
    "digit": 0.030,
    "punct": -0.025,  # punctuation and symbols
    "space": -0.015,  # spaces and tabs only
    "newline": -0.035,  # tokens containing a line break
}


def kind(text: str) -> str:
    if text.strip() == "":
        return "newline" if "\n" in text else "space"
    if text.strip().isdigit():
        return "digit"
    if text.strip().isalpha():
        return "letter"
    return "punct"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    return carry, MEAN_BY_KIND[kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Verb slot after a modal verb.

The component fires on the word that sits in the bare-verb slot of a modal
construction: the word right after "can", "could", "will", "may", "should",
"must", ... ("can [be]", "could [be] converted", "will [be] able", "can [also]
export"), and on the verb after an infinitive "to" ("to [establish]").
Adverbs or negation between the modal and the verb are skipped ("can also
[make]", "can't [do]"). The modal itself fires moderately, and a verb two or
three words after a modal fires weakly. Chinese and Russian modal verbs count
too. Everything else is predicted as 0.
"""

import wordnet

READS = ()

# Modal verbs (English, Chinese, Russian); the modal itself fires about 6.
MODALS = {
    "can", "could", "will", "would", "should", "may", "might", "must", "shall", "cannot",
    "可以", "能够", "可能", "要", "能", "会", "需要", "может", "можно", "могут", "должна", "должен", "будет", "можете",
}

# How strongly the word after each modal (or after "to", "be", "need", ...) fires.
FOLLOW = {
    "can": 8.5, "could": 8.5, "may": 7.4, "should": 7.2, "will": 6.9, "might": 6.9, "would": 6.2,
    "shall": 5.8, "must": 5.6, "'ll": 5.5, "cannot": 6.9,
    "be": 4.2, "need": 4.1, "want": 4.1, "let": 2.8, "going": 3.4, "likely": 3.4, "unable": 4.7,
    "to": 2.7,
    "可以": 7.1, "能够": 9.2, "可能": 5.9, "要": 5.7, "需要": 4.3, "能": 3.2, "会": 3.1, "将": 2.8,
    "может": 7.8, "можно": 6.9, "могут": 8.0,
}

# Words that can sit between a modal and its verb.
ADVERBS = {
    "also", "still", "now", "even", "just", "only", "not", "never", "always", "really", "then",
    "easily", "well", "all", "often", "simply", "further", "first", "again", "ever", "probably",
    "definitely", "certainly", "actually",
}

TAIL = {2: 3.0, 3: 1.5}  # a verb this many words after a modal


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    words = [s.strip().lower() for s in prefix.token_strings]
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = len(words) - 1

    def word_back(k):
        # the word k places back, if it is in the same document
        j = t - k
        return words[j] if j >= 0 and docs[j] == docs[t] else ""

    cur = words[t]
    if cur in MODALS:
        return carry, 6.0
    k = 1
    while word_back(k) in ADVERBS:
        k += 1
    before = word_back(k)
    # the verb slot: after a modal, or after "to" when the word is a verb
    if before in FOLLOW and (before != "to" or "verb" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(cur)):
        return carry, FOLLOW[before]
    if "verb" in wordnet.parts_of_speech(cur):
        for d in (2, 3):
            if word_back(d) in MODALS:
                return carry, TAIL[d]
    return carry, 0.0

"""Explainer for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3211 (a weak, mostly unexplained feature).

What it seems to respond to: positions in expository sentences that say what a concept or
technique is, what it is used for, or how important it is. The largest activations fall on
a copula or auxiliary opening such a generic statement ("moral hazard [is]", "Cookies have
[been] used") or on a usefulness word itself ("important", "used", "role", "technology").
Activations are lower on dialogue, chat and code, and on pronoun subjects. Read through the
unembedding, its output direction promotes continuations such as "used for", "applications",
"popular" and "usage".

What this program does: it scores each token from two word lists and a running topic
density, and nothing else:
  - a usefulness word (important, useful, used, role, technology, ...) adds a large amount;
  - a copula or auxiliary verb (is, are, has, been, can, ...) adds a smaller amount;
  - the decayed density of usefulness words earlier in the document (reset at each new
    document) adds more when the text has been talking about uses and importance.
It explains very little of the variance: about 0.7% on the eval rows (r = 0.09). For
comparison, a per-token lookup table reached about 2% on training rows, and a small GRU
over tokens about 5%. Most of the component's variation depends on context this program
does not model.
"""
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

USE_WORDS = frozenset(
    "important useful used use uses role popular application applications tool tools "
    "technique techniques technology theory industry particularly especially often "
    "typically usually common known".split()
)
COPULAS = frozenset("is are was were has have had been be can become becomes".split())
DECAY = 0.98


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    m, n = (0.0, 0.0) if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    topic = m / (n + 1.0)
    use = 1.0 if word in USE_WORDS else 0.0
    cop = 1.0 if word in COPULAS else 0.0
    value = 0.05 + 0.3 * cop + 0.7 * use + 4.0 * topic
    return (DECAY * m + use, DECAY * n + 1.0), float(value)

"""Explainer program for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3212.

What it does: a weak, dense readout. Its activation is positive in mathematical text about
transformations and scaling (rotations, ratios, matrices, linear maps, symmetries, scale
factors) and in mathematical notation, and negative in code and tool-call text. Most
tokens sit near zero. This program predicts it from a weighted list of those words, plus a
running average of the same signal over the current document, which restarts at each new
document. It captures only a little of the variance: most of the component's variation is
not explained by word identity or topic.
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# How strongly each word of transformation and scaling mathematics pushes the activation up.
WORD_WEIGHT = {
    "rotation": 3.0,
    "ratio": 2.0,
    "transformation": 2.0,
    "transform": 1.0,
    "matrix": 1.5,
    "symmetry": 1.3,
    "scale": 0.9,
    "linear": 0.8,
    "map": 0.7,
    "mapping": 0.7,
    "factor": 0.6,
    "operator": 0.8,
    "translation": 0.8,
    "reflection": 1.0,
    "isometry": 1.0,
    "similarity": 0.8,
}
# Mathematical notation: LaTeX dollar, backslash, super- and subscripts, braces, roots, Greek.
NOTATION = re.compile(r"[$\\^_{}√]|[α-ωΑ-Ω]")
# Code and tool-call text, where the activation is negative.
CODE = re.compile(r"^(_+|user|arguments|execute|exit|cat)$")

DECAY = 0.97  # per-token decay of the running averages within a document


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word_avg, notation_avg, doc = (0.0, 0.0, None) if carry is None else carry
    if prefix.document_ids[-1] != doc:  # a new document: forget the running averages
        word_avg, notation_avg = 0.0, 0.0
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    weight = WORD_WEIGHT.get(word, 0.0)
    is_notation = 1.0 if NOTATION.search(token) else 0.0
    is_code = 1.0 if CODE.match(word) else 0.0
    # The current token's word weight, the document's recent word weight, its recent
    # notation density, minus code.
    value = 0.4 * weight + 4.0 * word_avg + 0.2 * notation_avg - 0.6 * is_code
    word_avg = DECAY * word_avg + (1 - DECAY) * weight
    notation_avg = DECAY * notation_avg + (1 - DECAY) * is_notation
    return (word_avg, notation_avg, prefix.document_ids[-1]), value

"""Component p-82af68dd@100000/layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3213 (layer 15 MLP, down_proj).

Plain-terms summary: quiet on ordinary words, negative on formatting and on repeated text.
Its activation goes negative when:
  - the token is a line break or tab (strongest kind offset), or punctuation or a symbol;
  - the text is copying an earlier passage: the last few tokens already occurred earlier in
    this document, and the longer the repeated run, the more negative;
  - the current line so far matches the start of an earlier line in this document, with
    digits treated as interchangeable (numbered listings, repeated log lines, test output).
Ordinary words sit near zero, and the first token of a row is zero.

Per document the program keeps, in its carry: the recent tokens, every run of up to 8 tokens
seen so far, and every line prefix seen so far. Digits are read as one placeholder in both
lookups, so "Test 4:" repeats "Test 5:".

Fitted by least squares on 2048 training rows; out-of-sample variance explained about 0.17.
"""

import re

READS = ()

MAX_RUN = 8
"""Longest run of recent tokens checked for an earlier copy."""

KIND_OFFSET = {
    "newline": -0.89,  # whitespace containing a line break or tab
    "space": 0.06,  # other whitespace
    "digit": 0.12,
    "punct": -0.16,  # punctuation and symbols
    "other": -0.05,
    "word": 0.0,  # ordinary words: the baseline
}
"""Mean activation offset by the kind of the current token."""

COPY_BASE, COPY_PER_RUN = -0.07, -0.08
"""A copied run of 2+ tokens adds COPY_BASE + COPY_PER_RUN * run length."""

REPEATED_LINE = -1.93
"""Added when the current line so far matches the start of an earlier line."""

DIGIT = "<digit>"
"""The placeholder every digit token is read as in the copy and line lookups."""


def kind_of(text):
    """The kind of a token, from its own text."""
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s+", text):
        return "newline" if re.search(r"[\n\t]", text) else "space"
    if re.fullmatch(r" ?[A-Za-z]+", text):
        return "word"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s?[0-9]+", text):
        return "digit"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s?[^\w\s]+", text):
        return "punct"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """The component's activation at the newest token of `prefix`."""
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    kind = kind_of(text)
    key = DIGIT if kind == "digit" else prefix.token_ids[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry["doc"] != doc:
        carry = {"doc": doc, "keys": [], "runs": set(), "line": [], "lines": set()}
    keys = carry["keys"]
    keys.append(key)

    # Longest run of recent tokens that already occurred earlier in this document.
    longest = min(len(keys), MAX_RUN)
    run = 0
    for k in range(1, longest + 1):
        if tuple(keys[-k:]) in carry["runs"]:
            run = k
        else:
            break
    for k in range(1, longest + 1):
        carry["runs"].add(tuple(keys[-k:]))

    # Does the current line so far match the start of an earlier line?
    line = carry["line"]
    line.append(key)
    repeated = tuple(line) in carry["lines"]
    for k in range(1, len(line) + 1):
        carry["lines"].add(tuple(line[:k]))
    if "\n" in text:
        carry["line"] = []

    if prefix.position == 0:
        return carry, 0.0
    value = KIND_OFFSET[kind]
    if run >= 2:
        value += COPY_BASE + COPY_PER_RUN * run
    if repeated:
        value += REPEATED_LINE
    return carry, value


if __name__ == "__main__":
    # A quick look: the activation the program gives each character of a short text.
    class _Prefix:
        def __init__(self, ids, strings, docs):
            self.token_ids, self.token_strings, self.document_ids = ids, strings, docs
            self.position = len(ids) - 1

    demo = "Test 4: ok\nTest 5: ok\nTest 6: ok\nThe cat sat."
    strings = [demo[i : i + 1] for i in range(len(demo))]
    ids = [ord(c) for c in demo]
    state = None
    for t in range(len(ids)):
        p = _Prefix(ids[: t + 1], strings[: t + 1], [0] * (t + 1))

    if regex.fullmatch(r"\p{P}+", word) or word in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        return -0.3
    if regex.fullmatch(r"\p{L}+", word):

    return -0.05


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    """One position: track whether we are inside an assistant reply, then predict."""
    # carry: (inside_assistant_reply, expecting_role_word) for the current document.
    new_doc = len(prefix.document_ids) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    inside, pending = (False, False) if carry is None or new_doc else carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous = "" if new_doc else prefix.token_strings[-2]

        inside = token.strip() == "assistant"
        pending = False
    elif token == "<|im_end|>":
        inside = False

Its activation is large on the preposition "by" (and "By") when "by" introduces an
agent or a means after a verb: "designed by", "funded by", "classified by", "By default",
"By the way". It is near zero on every other token, which carry only small diffuse
noise (std about 0.3) that no simple rule here captures.

Within "by", two kinds read weaker: arithmetic ("divided by", "multiplied by",
"step by"), which is close to zero, and "by" after a verb of accompaniment, cause or
description ("followed by", "caused by", "characterized by", "surrounded by"), which is
about a quarter of the agent level.

READS = ()

ARITHMETIC = {"divide", "divided", "divisible", "multiply", "multiplied", "multiplying", "times", "step"}
ACCOMPANIMENT_OR_CAUSE = {
    "accompanied", "affected", "caused", "characterized", "followed", "governed",
    "influenced", "inspired", "required", "surrounded",
}

AGENT_LEVEL = 1.9  # "by" after most verbs, and at the start of a sentence
ARITHMETIC_LEVEL = 0.1
WEAK_LEVEL = 0.5
OTHER_LEVEL = 0.02  # mean of every other token


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower() != "by":
        return carry, OTHER_LEVEL
    same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]

What it does, in plain terms: this component's activation is large and positive on the
word "by" when "by" introduces the agent or means of a passive verb ("determined by",
"made by", "obtained by", "described by"), and it is weaker on "by" in other uses.
It is near zero on "by" in fixed idioms with no agent ("divided by", "followed by",
"step by step", "accompanied by"), and near zero on almost every other token.
The same feature fires on "by"-like words in other languages ("por", "par", "durch").

The program predicts that rule: the group means measured on training text.
  - "by" after a past participle (word ending in "ed"): about 1.4
  - "by" after anything else: about 2.0
  - "by" in the no-agent idioms: 0
  - every other token: 0 (the component's mean over other tokens is about 0.03)

Limits: this captures only about 3% of the activation's variance. Most of the rest is
diffuse, small, context-dependent noise that no word list explains. The remaining
signal is a weak negative on the second word of contrasting pairs ("physical and
[mental]", "male and [female]"), mostly adjective-adjective coordinations, which a
word-class rule barely improves on and which is left out here.

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# "by"-like prepositions: English, plus Portuguese/French/German translations.
BY_WORDS = {"by", "por", "par", "durch"}

# Idioms where "by" has no agent: "divided by", "followed by", "step by step".
NO_AGENT_BEFORE = {"divided", "followed", "multiplied", "step", "accompanied", "side", "sides", "divisible"}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()

What it does, in plain terms: the component is positive on a common-noun word that
comes straight after another noun or adjective, the way the head of a compound noun
phrase does in technical prose ("participation rate", "modelling method", "survival
rate", "analytical method"). It is negative on a noun that comes straight after a
determiner ("the rate", "a method"). Other words are near zero, with a small positive
lean for verbs and adjectives.

The program follows that rule with word classes from WordNet and a fixed set of
determiners, and predicts a small value per position. It captures only a little of
the component's variance: most of its activation is diffuse context that no word
class explains.
"""

import functools

import wordnet

READS = ()

DETERMINERS = frozenset(
    "a an the this that these those its their his her our your my each every some "
    "any no all both such another one".split()
)

# Predicted activation for each class of word.
NOUN_AFTER_MODIFIER = 0.20  # head noun right after a noun or adjective
NOUN_AFTER_DETERMINER = -0.15  # noun right after a/the/this/...
OTHER_NOUN = 0.05  # any other word-initial noun
VERB = 0.07  # word-initial verb that is not also a noun
OTHER_WORD = 0.02  # other word-initial alphabetic word


@functools.lru_cache(maxsize=None)
def _classes(token):
    """(is_noun, is_adjective, is_verb) for a word, from WordNet; all False otherwise."""
    word = token.strip().lower()
    if not word.isalpha():
        return (False, False, False)
    senses = wordnet.parts_of_speech(word)
    return ("noun" in senses, "adjective" in senses, "verb" in senses)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    if len(prefix.token_strings) < 2 or prefix.document_ids[-2] != prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        previous = ""  # first token of a document: no left context
    else:
        previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    if not token.startswith(" "):
        return carry, 0.0  # only word-initial tokens (a leading space) count as words
    is_noun, _, is_verb = _classes(token)
    if is_noun:
        prev_word = previous.strip().lower()
        if prev_word in DETERMINERS:
            return carry, NOUN_AFTER_DETERMINER
        prev_noun, prev_adj, _ = _classes(previous) if prev_word else (False, False, False)
        if prev_noun or prev_adj:
            return carry, NOUN_AFTER_MODIFIER
        return carry, OTHER_NOUN
    if is_verb:
        return carry, VERB
    return carry, OTHER_WORD

"""Layer 15 MLP hidden unit 3233 (the component's activation), as a position-in-document baseline.

What the unit does is not captured by any simple rule. Its activation is spread
across contexts with no clear token, word-class, script, repetition, or
surprisal pattern. The only stable regularity found is positional: the first
token of a document is near zero, the next few tokens sit slightly higher, and
the level decays toward its long-run mean (about 0.03) within a few dozen tokens.

This program predicts exactly that: 0 at each document's first token, and
0.027 + 0.09 * exp(-(k - 1) / 10) at the k-th token of a document (k >= 1).
It explains almost none of the variance; it is a baseline, not an explanation.
"""
import math
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

MEAN = 0.027  # long-run mean activation
BUMP = 0.09  # extra level just after a document starts
DECAY = 10.0  # tokens over which the extra level fades


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    # k: index of this token within its document (0 at a document's first token)
    if carry is None or prefix.position == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]:
        k = 0
    else:
        k = carry + 1
    if k == 0:
        return k, 0.0
    return k, MEAN + BUMP * math.exp(-(k - 1) / DECAY)

"""Trouble-talk detector for component 3234 of layers.15.mlp.down_proj.

Plain-language reading: the component's output direction promotes words like
"malfunction", "glitches", "errors", "faulty", "broken" (its logit-lens read-out).
In the data it is most active on words about something breaking, failing or glitching
(e.g. "lost", "breaking", "issues", "broken"), and it stays mildly positive for the next
16 tokens. It dips slightly negative inside code and library identifiers.

The values below are group means measured on training text. Most of the component's
variance is token-level noise that no reading of the text captures, so this program
explains only a little of it (about 0.1% of variance on held-out eval rows).
"""

import re
from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words about something breaking, failing, glitching or being unreliable (English and Chinese).
TROUBLE = re.compile(
    r"glitch|freez|crash|reload|replay|playback|buffer|interrupt|intermitt|error|issue|"
    r"problem|broke|broken|break|fail|malfunction|fault|troubl|stuck|lost|unable|"
    r"unfortunat|cache|blurry|flicker|disconnect|reconnect|outage|bug|"
    r"故障|问题|毛病|失灵|出错|异常|失误|不能|不行|坏"
)
# Code-like tokens: brackets, operators, underscores, dotted or camelCase identifiers.
CODE = re.compile(r"[{}();=<>\[\]_/\\.:]|[a-z][A-Z]")

WINDOW = 16  # tokens after a trouble word that still count as "still about the trouble"
TROUBLE_VALUE = 0.44  # on the trouble word itself
WINDOW_VALUE = 0.035  # within WINDOW tokens after one
CODE_VALUE = -0.026  # code-like tokens elsewhere
OTHER_VALUE = 0.015  # everything else


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    """Activation at the newest token, from the tokens so far in its document."""
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    since, last_doc = carry if carry is not None else (WINDOW + 1, None)
    if doc != last_doc:  # a new document: forget earlier trouble
        since = WINDOW + 1
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1].lower()
    if TROUBLE.search(token):
        return (0, doc), TROUBLE_VALUE
    since += 1  # tokens since the last trouble word
    if since <= WINDOW:
        return (since, doc), WINDOW_VALUE
    if CODE.search(token):
        return (since, doc), CODE_VALUE
    return (since, doc), OTHER_VALUE

before them (e.g. "a" in "a unique", "an" in "an individual"). A prefix-only program cannot

and not captured by any word list, so this program explains only a small part of it.

individuality word a fixed strength. Stems are matched in English, Russian, German,

    ("personaliz", 8), ("personalis", 8), ("customiz", 6), ("customis", 6), ("bespoke", 10),

    if word in EXACT:

that writes a negative signal. It is nearly silent on ordinary prose and code. It goes
strongly negative on the line break that ends a markdown heading, such as the "\\n\\n" after

tokens, and its last non-space character. Documents packed into one row are kept apart.

activation is noisy within each class (sd about 8 after headings), and the many small
contributions from ordinary tokens are not modelled, so this explains about 15% of the
variance.

READS = ()

HASHES = {"#", "##", "###", "####", "#####", "######"}  # a markdown heading marker alone
SENTENCE_END = set(".!?,;:)\"'*`")  # punctuation that ends a sentence or clause


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:  # a new document starts a new line

captures only about 1% of the variance; most of it is context the program does not see.
"""

import re

READS = ()

# Average activation of each token kind on training text.
MEAN = {
    "newline": -0.111,
    "space": -0.119,
    "space_word": -0.028,
    "word": -0.061,
    "cjk": -0.016,
    "digit": -0.085,
    "punct": -0.101,
    "other": -0.086,
}


def kind(text):
    """The kind of one token, from its text."""
    if re.search(r"[\n\r]", text):
        return "newline"
    if re.fullmatch(r"\s+", text):
        return "space"
    if re.fullmatch(r" [A-Za-z]+", text):
        return "space_word"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z_0-9]*", text):
        return "word"
    if re.search(r"[　-鿿가-힯]", text):
        return "cjk"
    if re.search(r"\d", text):
        return "digit"
    if re.fullmatch(r"[^\w\s]+", text):
        return "punct"
    return "other"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN[kind(prefix.token_strings[-1])]

"""Quantity-context predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj component 3259.

What the component does, as far as text shows: it reads one MLP hidden unit of layer 15
(mainly unit 3259) and writes a small amount into the residual stream. Its largest
activations come in prose about physical quantities and motion: a block that is "pushed
down", a "one-quarter turn", "how far" to rotate, a speed, a distance, an angular
acceleration, a depth, a score "up to" some number. Its most negative values come in
legal, ontology and code text. Most of its variance is not explained by any word or topic
we could name: token identity explains nothing on held-out text.

This program predicts a small positive value at a token that is itself a quantity or
motion word, plus a smaller one for each quantity word among the 32 tokens before it in the
same document, and a constant floor otherwise. It is a conceptual sketch of the top
contexts, not a good fit: it explains about 0.1% of the variance.
"""

from collections.abc import Mapping

READS: tuple[str, ...] = ()

# Words for physical quantities, motion and rotation, magnitudes and units.
QUANTITY_WORDS = frozenset(
    """speed velocity distance displacement depth height width length angle angular
    rotation rotate rotated turn degrees far position acceleration force torque mass
    voltage current temperature amplitude pressure frequency units unit meters inches
    feet points score duty radius volume weight percent rate moved move moving pushed
    pulled push pull up down deeper higher lower compress stretch amount quantity time
    seconds hours minutes""".split()
)

WINDOW = 32  # tokens of context looked back over, within the same document
BASE, OWN, CONTEXT = -0.026, 0.12, 0.13  # intercept, current token, fraction in window


def _is_quantity(token: str) -> bool:
    return token.strip().lower() in QUANTITY_WORDS


def step(carry, prefix, upstream: Mapping):
    t = prefix.position
    doc = prefix.document_ids[t]
    lo = max(0, t - WINDOW)
    before = [
        prefix.token_strings[i]
        for i in range(lo, t)
        if prefix.document_ids[i] == doc
    ]
    share = sum(_is_quantity(s) for s in before) / max(1, len(before))
    own = _is_quantity(prefix.token_strings[t])
    return carry, BASE + OWN * own + CONTEXT * share

"""Constant predictor for layers.15.mlp.down_proj:3260.

This component is (almost exactly) the output of MLP hidden unit 3260 in layer 15,
scaled by its write norm. Its activation is diffuse and heavy-tailed: its sign and
size depend on deep, context-dependent computation, and no token identity, neighbouring
token, character class, repetition or document-level feature I tested explains it.
So the best simple program predicts its average value at every position.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.0340  # mean over 4096 training rows x 512 positions


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3261: a constant predictor.

This component's activation is a linear readout of the layer-15 MLP's hidden units
(its direction is dominated by hidden unit 3261, then spread over thousands of small
weights). It has no concept a reader can name: its value does not follow the current
token, the previous token, the token's class (punctuation, digits, words, whitespace),
or the position in the document, and its harvested windows are empty because its CI never
passes the threshold. The best readable predictor is therefore the component's typical
value, which is its mean, about 0.035, at every position.
"""

READS = ()

MEAN_ACTIVATION = 0.035


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, MEAN_ACTIVATION

"""Layer 15 MLP down_proj, component 3262: a weak, diffuse contributor with no
readable trigger, so this program predicts 0 everywhere.

What the component is: it reads the MLP hidden state through one input direction
v (about a quarter of its squared norm is MLP hidden unit 3262 itself) and writes
along one 2048-dim residual direction u. Its activation is (hidden . v) * |u|,
with std 0.31 and mean about 0, and it almost never passes causal importance
(0 of 10M tokens above 0.1). Switching it off barely changes the model's output.

What was tried, on about 2M training tokens, to find a readable rule for the
activation, each explaining under 2% of its variance on held-out tokens:
  - the token's identity (a lookup of mean activation per token),
  - the previous token's identity,
  - the token's class (word, punctuation, CJK, Cyrillic, digit, with or without a
    leading space),
  - the class of the next token,
  - position in the document (the spread grows from 0 at the first token to about
    0.1 after 64 tokens, but the sign does not follow any position rule),
  - whether the token already occurred earlier in its document.
The strongest single correlate is hidden unit 3262 (r = 0.51), and that unit is
driven by context, not by any token class. The positive side seems to fall on
words that a noun phrase continues (for example "other", "general", "personal"),
and the negative side on commas, full stops and "born" after a name, but no rule
captured it.

So the program predicts a constant 0. Its variance explained is about zero by
design: a token table would add about 1% and would need arbitrary token ids.
"""

READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    return carry, 0.0

"""Layer 15 MLP, component 3263 (down_proj), predicted as a near-constant.

What the component is: a rank-one piece of layer 15's down projection. Its read
direction is almost entirely hidden unit 3263 of that MLP (about 42% of its squared
norm sits on that unit; the rest is spread thinly over thousands of units). Its
activation is a dense, signed, roughly symmetric value: mean about 0.05, std about 0.3.
Measured on training text, no simple token, character-class, position or
preceding-context rule explains more than about 1% of its variance on held-out rows.

What this program does: it predicts the component's typical value, about 0.047, at every
position, except the first token of each document, where the component is essentially 0.
It is a baseline. It does not explain the component's variance.
"""

READS = ()

TYPICAL = 0.047  # mean activation at non-initial positions in training text


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    first_in_doc = len(docs) == 1 or docs[-1] != docs[-2]
    return carry, 0.0 if first_in_doc else TYPICAL
